problem_statement: A device whose driver API embeds another (parent) driver API as its first member should be recognisable as belonging to the parent API class. DEVICE_API_IS(parent_class, dev) must return true for a device whose API is a child class that extends the parent, and DEVICE_API_GET/DEVICE_API_IS must work correctly for multi-level inheritance (grandchild extends child extends parent) and for sibling relationships (two child classes extending the same parent must be distinguished, and a sibling must not be recognised as the other child). Before this capability a child-class device is not seen as a member of the parent class, so a device using an extended API cannot be used wherever the base API is expected.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/kernel/device -s tests/kernel/device/kernel.device -s kernel.device -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The problem statement describes the desired behaviour of DEVICE_API_IS and DEVICE_API_GET for inheritance but omits the name and signature of the macro (DEVICE_API_EXTENDS) that the tests use to declare the parent-child relationship, which the agent must implement.

problems.detail: The hidden tests use the macro DEVICE_API_EXTENDS(_child, _parent, _member) to declare the parent-child API relationship, but the problem statement never mentions this macro by name, its parameter list, or its purpose. Without it the agent cannot implement the macro that the test header (abstract_driver.h) calls, so the tests would not compile.

problem_statement_fixed: A device whose driver API embeds another (parent) driver API as its first member should be recognisable as belonging to the parent API class. The relationship is declared with the macro DEVICE_API_EXTENDS(_child, _parent, _member), where _child is the name of the child (extending) API class, _parent is the name of the parent (base) API class, and _member is the name of the first member of the child API struct whose type is the parent API struct. DEVICE_API_IS(parent_class, dev) must return true for a device whose API is a child class that extends the parent, and DEVICE_API_GET/DEVICE_API_IS must work correctly for multi-level inheritance (grandchild extends child extends parent) and for sibling relationships (two child classes extending the same parent must be distinguished, and a sibling must not be recognised as the other child). Before this capability a child-class device is not seen as a member of the parent class, so a device using an extended API cannot be used wherever the base API is expected.
